grades.question: What makes a normal move legal, can the same warriors move repeatedly, and do rivers count as paths?
grades.expected_answer: Move more than zero warriors/pawns along one linking path to an adjacent clearing; rule origin or destination or both. Same pieces can move repeatedly. Rivers are not paths unless explicitly treated as such.

grades.question: Describe battle from ambush through removal: foiling, early ending, dice limits, extra hits, removal priorities and who scores removed buildings/tokens.
grades.expected_answer: Defender may ambush matching clearing; attacker may foil with matching ambush. Unfoiled ambush deals two immediate hits; discard defender ambush, end battle if no attacking warriors/pawns remain. Before-roll effects, roll high attacker/low defender, rolled hits capped by own warriors, after-roll effects, count hits including uncapped extra hits and defenseless extra attacker hit if no defending warriors, then deal hits. Each side chooses own removals, warriors first. Whoever removes enemy building/token scores one, including defender.

observed.answer: Battle order: defender may play one matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. The defender's ambush is discarded; if foiled it deals no hits, otherwise it deals two immediate hits, not capped by defending warriors. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Resolve before-roll effects, roll (higher die is attacker's hits, lower is defender's; Alliance defending reverses dice), then resolve after-roll effects. Rolled hits are capped by each side's own warriors in battle, except Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Add extra hits without a warrior cap and subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker gets one defenseless hit; Vagabond is defenseless only with no undamaged swords. For each side's removals, its owner chooses the order, but all warriors must be removed before buildings/tokens; hits are dealt by both sides and losing warriors does not change the roll cap retroactively. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, including a defender and outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.
observed.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle: Battle (4.3), six steps.

grades.question: When does Outrage trigger, what is paid, and what if the player has no matching card or the supporter stack is full?

observed.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card, with birds counting; moving a group costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, and the Alliance draws one card from the deck into Supporters. The supporter capacity still applies, so incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded. The summary gives the no-card fallback, but does not specify a different payment if the supporter stack is full beyond this capacity rule.

grades.question: How do Alliance Revolt and Spread Sympathy differ in timing/order, eligible clearing, supporter cost, martial law and results?
grades.expected_answer: Birdsong Revolt before Spread, each any number. Revolt: sympathetic clearing without base whose matching base is on board, pay two matching supporters, remove all enemy pieces, place matching base, warriors equal matching sympathetic clearings, one officer, score removed enemy buildings/tokens. Spread: unsympathetic adjacent to sympathy or any clearing if none; pay shown matching supporters plus one if at least three warriors of one other player; place sympathy and score uncovered points.

observed.answer: In Birdsong, the Alliance may Revolt any number of times first, then Spread Sympathy any number of times. Revolt selects a sympathetic clearing with no base matching a base still on its board, spends two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces there, places the matching base, places warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit, and places one warrior in the Officers box. It scores normal VP for enemy buildings/tokens removed; an enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed. Spread Sympathy selects an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if there is no sympathy, and spends the supporter cost shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter for Martial Law if any one other player has at least three warriors there. It places sympathy and scores the uncovered track VP. Only one sympathy per clearing; the Keep's placement ban applies. The summary says Revolt uses two matching supporters and Spread Sympathy uses the listed cost plus any Martial Law supporter; it does not give a separate numeric base cost for each specific token.

grades.question: How do Vagabond refresh, Slip, normal Move and forest Rest work, including hostile destinations and Evening drawing?
grades.expected_answer: Refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on track, then three more; newly refreshed tea does not boost that step. observed.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh then. Slip is optional and moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out of a clearing. A normal Vagabond move exhausts one boot, plus one extra boot if the destination has any warriors of a Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. In Evening, if in a forest, Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, but does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. The Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on its track, even after Rest.

grades.question: When does a faction become Hostile to Vagabond, when is Infamy scored, can Aid undo Hostility, and what does Strike target?
grades.expected_answer: Removing any one non-hostile faction warrior makes Hostile. Infamy one extra VP per hostile piece removed in battle during own turn except warrior causing hostility; no Infamy for Strike. Aid cannot undo hostility but can take crafted item. Strike exhaust crossbow, removes enemy warrior, or other faction piece if that enemy has no warriors there.

observed.answer: Removing one warrior of a faction that is not already Hostile immediately makes that faction Hostile to the Vagabond, except the special allied battle-loss case. During battle on the Vagabond's own turn, Infamy scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior whose removal first made that faction Hostile; ordinary building/token removal VP also applies. There is no Infamy while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile relationship out of Hostile, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors in the clearing may it instead remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and scores no Infamy.

grades.question: What are coalition eligibility, timing, VP requirement, partner selection and victory, and what changes if partner is Hostile?
grades.expected_answer: Vagabond cannot use normal dominance win. With four or more players during own Daylight at least 10 VP activates dominance to coalition with lowest VP other player not already in coalition, choose tied lowest. Place score marker on partner board, stop scoring; partner win means Vagabond also wins. Hostile partner relationship becomes Indifferent.

observed.answer: The Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance. With four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to form a coalition with a player not already in a coalition, choosing a player with the lowest VP among players other than itself (choosing among ties). It places its score marker on that player's faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, the Vagabond also wins, including when the partner wins by dominance. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
